rows.assumption: A-1: "5 MWh" means usable thermal energy stored (MWh_th)
A-2: The storage medium is "solar salt" (60% NaNO3, 40% KNO3)
A-3: The design is two tanks, one hot and one cold, with the salt pumped between them
A-4: The salt operates between 288 °C (cold) and 566 °C (hot)
A-5: Stored sensible heat = m·cp·ΔT
A-6: cp stays at 1.53 J/(g·K) across 288–566 °C
A-7: 85% of the salt inventory is usable (range 80–92%); the rest is a "heel" left in the tank so the pumps stay submerged
A-8: Each tank's height equals its diameter (H = D), with 10% freeboard, and the cold tank is built the same size as the hot tank
A-9: Tank wall thickness is set by fabrication minimums (6–12 mm), not by the pressure of the salt
A-10: Unit prices for salt, fabricated steel, pumps, piping, controls, insulation and foundations
A-11: Indirect costs (EPC margin, engineering, commissioning, contingency) multiply the direct cost by 1.35 (range 1.25–1.50)
A-12: Scope excludes the charging heater, the discharge heat exchanger and any power block
A-13: Life is 30 years at 365 full cycles a year (low case: 20 years at 300 cycles a year)
A-14: Heat is lost continuously with both tanks at full temperature and 25 °C ambient; a 1.5× factor covers foundations, nozzles and piping
A-15: Levelisation covers capital only, uses a 7% real discount rate, excludes O&M and charging energy, and is in 2026 USD
A-16: Salt density follows ρ = 2090 − 0.636·T(°C) kg/m³
A-17: Every cycle delivers the full 5 MWh_th (surfaced in the Assumption Audit)
A-18: Charging energy costs more than about 2.4 ¢/kWh_th (surfaced in the Assumption Audit)
A-19: Roof framing, nozzles and internals add 1.3× to the shell steel (surfaced in the Assumption Audit)
A-20: Two pumps and 50 m of heat-traced piping are enough for 2.94 kg/s at a 4-hour discharge (surfaced in the Assumption Audit)

chains.title: Solar salt cycled from 288 to 566 °C stores 0.11815 kWh_th per kg, so it needs 8.4638 kg per kWh_th
The salt inventory of 49,787 kg costs $44,808, or $8.96/kWh_th (bracket $4.60–15.87)
Two tanks of 31.66 m³ each cost $113,786, or $22.76/kWh_th (bracket $10.36–59.71)
The lowest cost physics allows is about $3.84/kWh_th (salt alone), and the salt's pressure needs only 1.30 mm of shell
At 5 MWh_th, the salt is 12.1% of direct cost, and installed cost is 26× the lowest the physics allows
The store retains 92.0% of its heat per day on a one-cycle-per-day duty (bracket 90.0–93.9%)
Levelised capital cost is 0.99 ¢/kWh_th delivered undiscounted, or 2.40 ¢/kWh_th at 7% real (brackets 0.47–4.66 ¢ and 1.13–8.81 ¢)

conclusion.recommended: Use about $100/kWh_th of usable capacity ($99.94; $499,691 installed) as the central capital cost for a 5 MWh_th two-tank solar-salt store, and carry its bracket of $48–252/kWh_th with it (chain C5).
